title: Ofrenda comunitaria para día de los muertos / Community Ofrenda for Dia de los Muertos
description: nbsp;\nOur annual community ofrenda will be constructed the week leading up to Dia de los Muertos and the community is invited to view and participate.
parentSummary: nbsp;\nOur annual community ofrenda will be constructed the week leading up to Dia de los Muertos and the community is invited to view and participate.
sourceDescriptionRaw:
¡Pasa a ver, o contribuir a, la ofrenda comunitaria de la Biblioteca Latinoamericana! Nuestra ofrenda comunitaria anual se montará durante la semana previa al Día de los Muertos, y invitamos a toda la comunidad a visitarla y participar. Si nos visita en persona, puede dejar una pequeña foto o un recuerdo** de un ser querido fallecido para integrarlo al altar.
Las ofrendas o altares son una tradición central del Día de los Muertos en México. Por lo general, los familiares los preparan para dar la bienvenida simbólica a sus difuntos en estas fechas tan especiales.
**Recomendaciones importantes: Le sugerimos dejar fotografías o recuerdos en copia o en réplica, ya que el altar estará accesible al público durante todo el horario de apertura de la biblioteca. La Biblioteca Latinoamericana y la SJPL (Biblioteca Pública de San José) no se hacen responsables de artículos perdidos o dañados. Podrá recoger sus objetos en persona del 4 al 6 de noviembre. Los artículos no reclamados después del 6 de noviembre serán retirados.
Gratis. No se requiere registro.Stop by to view, or contribute to, Biblioteca Latinoamericana's community ofrenda!nbsp;
Our annual community ofrenda will be constructed the week leading up to Dia de los Muertos and the community is invited to view and participate. Community members stopping by in-person are welcome to leave a small memento or photo of a loved one who has passed** to be represented on the altar.nbsp;Ofrendas, or altars, arenbsp;traditionally created for the Mexican Día de los Muertos celebration. Generally created bynbsp;the family members of the person who has died, they arenbsp;intended to welcome the deceased to the altar setting during this special time.
**We recommend leaving replicas or copies on the altar as it will be accessible to public at all times while the library is open.nbsp;Biblioteca Latinoamericana SJPL are not responsible for lost/damaged items. Items may be picked up in-person between November 4 6; items not claimed by November 6, will be discarded.
Free. No registration required.

Come unwind and learn something new at our monthly crafternoon! No experience is necessary.Supplies will be provided, and you’re welcome to bring any of your own. In fact some of these crafts may benefit from your personal stash! The activities will be suitable for ages 10 and up. We will have project samples each day to help you visualize the end result.
Programs will be on the fourth Sunday of the month.nbsp;
• October – Cardboard Nichonbsp; Recommended items to bring: small images of a cherished item, symbol, memory, or a nbsp;nbsp;lovednbsp;one you miss.• November – Embossing Aluminum Food Charmsnbsp; nbsp;Recommended items to bring: colorful sharpies• December – Felt and Beaded Patchesnbsp; Recommended items to bring: old jewelry you don’t mind disassembling, beads, colorful nbsp; thread, loose buttons, scraps of fabric and lace.
¡Ven a relajarte y a aprender algo nuevo en nuestra tarde mensual de artesanías! No se necesita experiencia. Se proporcionarán los materiales, pero puedes traer los que quieras. De hecho, ¡algunas de estas artesanías pueden beneficiarse de tus propios materiales! Las actividades serán aptas para mayores de 10 años. Cada día tendremos ejemplos de proyectos para ayudarte a visualizar el resultado final. • Agosto – Paisaje de playa en collage
 • Septiembre – Pintura de hongos
• Octubre – Nicho de cartónnbsp;nbsp;Materiales recomendados para traer: imágenes pequeñas de un objeto preciado, un símbolo, un recuerdo o un ser querido al que extrañas. • Noviembre – Dijes de aluminio con relieve nbsp; Artículos recomendados para traer: marcadores Sharpie de colores, piensa en cuál es tu comida reconfortante • Diciembre – Parches de fieltro y cuentasnbsp; Artículos recomendados para traer: joyas viejas que no te importe desarmar, cuentas, hilo de colores, botones sueltos, retazos de tela y encaje.

sourceDescriptionRaw:
Create your own rock, paper, scissors game using Swift Playground! Everyone Can Code is a beginner’s course on using iPads to code and modify technology, such as online games. Students will be learning the basics of coding and implementing them through the modification of rock, paper, scissors. 
Everything needed for this course will be provided, but you are more than welcome to bring your own personal iPad with the free Swift Playgrounds app downloaded, especially if you want to save your work.
Free. Registration is recommended.
This series is taught in English only.
Registration closes at 12pm the day before class. However, if seats are still available, students in grades 3-6 can walk in on Saturday if they arrive before 3pm to sign in. Maximum class size is 25.
Although the class is scheduled from 3-4:30pm, students who finish their projects early are welcome to leave early.
ADA Accommodation Requests

title: Elizabeth Jun (Nuyujukian Lab) & Lavonna Mark (Giocomo Lab)
description: Her research interests lie in understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate together to perform computations and support a wide range of behaviors in different contexts.
parentSummary: Her research interests lie in understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate together to perform computations and support a wide range of behaviors in different contexts.
sourceDescriptionRaw: Today's seminar features two talks from MBCT Student Members, Stanford PhD Students Elizabeth Jun and Lavonna Mark Join our mailing list for MBCT Seminar announcements and updates about future events Investigating preserved neural motifs across and within tasks in premotor cortexAbstractMotor systems neuroscience studies how populations of motor cortical neurons coordinate to perform motor computations, but less is known about how large repertoires of movements are flexibly generated from a fixed set of fundamental motor computations. There is an emerging idea of conserved neural “modules”, or recurring neural activity patterns deploying computations through dynamics, that may serve as elementary building blocks for performing the same fundamental computation across a wide array of contexts. However, exactly what feature of neural dynamics is “recurring” and fundamentally conserved, if any, when performing the same motor computation within a wide range of reach sequence and kinematic contexts has yet to be shown and characterized empirically. To investigate this, we trained an animal implanted with a 96-channel Utah array in premotor cortex to perform 4 visually guided arm reaching motor tasks that are composed of unique combinations of 5 distinct motor processes (preparation, initiation, execution, hold, error correction) implemented in various reach conditions, where the same process can reappear across tasks and reappear again within tasks. This design allows us to test the hypothesis that premotor dynamics reuse conserved neural dynamics for performing the same motor computational process, but potentially implemented in different locations and orientations in population state space when reperformed across tasks, repeated in a sequence within tasks, and in different kinematic conditions. In this talk, I will explore systematically testing this hypothesis for all 5 motor processes to understand whether there are general organizing principles for premotor dynamics associated with deploying the same fundamental motor computation in a range of tasks, sequences, and kinematic contexts. Meet the SpeakerElizabeth Jun, PhD Student, Nuyujukian Lab, Stanford University Elizabeth Jun is a neuroscience PhD Candidate at Stanford University and NIH F31 Predoctoral Fellow funded through National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS). Her research interests lie in understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate together to perform computations and support a wide range of behaviors in different contexts. Specifically in her thesis work, advised by Dr. Paul Nuyujukian in the Brain Interfacing Laboratory, she aims to understand how the brain can flexibly support a wide range of complex movements that are supported by a fixed set of fundamental motor computations. She is interested in connecting features of high-dimensional population data to similar behaviors in different contexts, and exploring in general how high-dimensional population features relate back to properties of the neural circuit. View Profile State-dependent grid cell spatial mapsAbstractTo navigate, the brain requires an internal map of external space. The medial entorhinal cortex (MEC) plays an important role in generating this map, with spatial cells that encode speed, head-direction, and position. This map is not static, however: MEC neurons can shift the position or rate of their firing fields, a process termed remapping. Remapping occurs in response to external changes to the environment (its color, shape, size, or reward features) but was recently found to occur also spontaneously in an unchanging environment (Low et al., 2021). Why spatial maps reorganize in a stable environment remains unclear. In this talk, I will address two questions. First, what drives spontaneous remapping? I will show that transitions between grid cell maps track changes in the animal’s internal arousal state, and that optogenetically driving state transitions can evoke spatial remapping. Second, how does internal state shape spatial dynamics? Modeling the toroidal grid cell attractor dynamics in spontaneous and optogenetically-evoked map transitions reveals that each state’s map reflects a distinct strength and phase at which landmarks pin grid cell dynamics. Together, these results suggest the presence of state-dependent spatial maps in the MEC, in which internal state tunes how landmarks entrain intrinsic attractor dynamics. Meet the SpeakerLavonna Mark, PhD Student, Giocomo Lab, Stanford University Lavonna Mark is a PhD candidate in the Giocomo Lab. She is interested in how neural circuits can dynamically switch their coding properties across internal states. Prior to graduate school, she studied how arousal states influence visual coding and perception in the Cardin and Higley Labs at the Yale School of Medicine. As a PhD candidate, she is interested in how downstream navigational circuits integrate state-dependent signals to coordinate adaptive behavior. Her research combines Neuropixels recordings in mice navigating virtual reality, behavior videography, optogenetics, and fiber photometry with computational approaches (continuous attractor and state space models), the latter in collaboration with Scott Linderman. View Profile Continue the conversation: All attendees are invited to digest the seminar with a complimentary dinner with the speaker in the Theory Center after the seminar.

Join us for music, stories, and joyful playnbsp;at this storytime perfect for families with young children. Music and movement help our littlest learners develop their communication skills, their imagination, and their connection with the loving grown-ups in their lives. Let's sing!Free, with limited capacity.
Vehicle parking may be limited. A small number of strollers may be parked outside the Children's Room; no strollers in storytime, please.
Sensory Notes:
- Sound: This storytime will be noisy with singing, instruments, and pre-recorded music. Let the librarian know before storytime begins if you would like to borrow a pair of ear defenders for your child.
- Visuals: This storytime is usually very busy with lots of families moving around.
- Texture: This storytime sometimes includes the use of soft scarves, weighted beanbags, and other textured items. Children are always free to skip these activities if they prefer.
Need a social story? Email charlie.roos@lib.sccgov.org to request a digital social story to help your child feel prepared for storytime.

sourceDescriptionRaw:
Drop in on Tuesday afternoons in at 4:30 p.m. for a new STEaM adventure every week. Active engagement with STEaM promotes academic success.nbsp;
Topic list is subject to change, please check back or call the branch for up-to-date details. Suggested ages vary, please refer to individual program descriptions.
Free, with limited capacity. Tickets will be distributed starting 60 minutes before the program.
Aug 18 -nbsp;The Science of Soap: Floating Drawing Pepper ExperimentParticipants will learn about the properties of soap, how it cleans and why that's important by creating their own floating drawings and playing with adhesion and repulsion properties of pepper and soap.
Aug 25 -nbsp;nbsp;Logic GamesWork individually or in teams to solve a variety of logic puzzles.***please note that the Mental Math: Multiplication program has been RESCHEDULED for Sept 22 and the other math topics have moved accordingly***
Sept 1 -nbsp;Marble Run FunHarness the force of gravity as you create your own marble run.
Sept 8 - Lego Engineering Challenge (***please note topic change***)In this workshop, children will be encouraged to build and solve problems. Children will learn to brainstorm and build with Lego® bricks, and then to redesign and build as they face challenges. For children ages 5 and up.
 Volcanoes (will be rescheduled at a later time)Learn about the different types of volcanoes and create your own eruption with common household ingredients.
Sept 15 - Spike Robotics Code Quest Learn to code a pre-built Lego Spike robot to move around and collect components using a block-based coding language similar to Scratch.
Sept 22 -nbsp;Mental Math:nbsp;MultiplicationChildren have the opportunity to learn and practice multiplication skills with a focus on understanding how multiplication works and is related to addition.
Oct 6 - Wind Turbine EngineeringIn this hands-on workshop, participants will build their own working wind turbines using everyday household items. Through fun, interactive experiments, they will test different designs and observe the impact of tweakable variables on performance. Lesson by Nurturing Young Mindz Foundation.
Oct 13 - Paper RocketsLearn what makes rockets fly high and far! Then join us in making a rocket of your own that can fly the furthest!nbsp;Participants will learn about propulsion and list then create their own rockets.
Oct 20 -nbsp;Properties of Water (Science from Scientists)Participants will explore cohesion, adhesion andnbsp;surface tension through a series of simple activities that encourage them to investigate and make observations about the unique propertiesnbsp;of water.
Free, with limited capacity. Tickets will be distributed starting 60 minutes before the program. Children younger than age 9 must be accompanied by an adult caregiver during this program.
Oct 27 - TBA

Nov 10 - Ozobot Maze RunnerTeach your Ozobot to navigate a maze using simple color codes.
Nov 17 -nbsp;Logic GamesWork individually or in teams to solve a variety of logic puzzles.
Nov 24nbsp;-nbsp;TBA

They will participate in fun parachute drops with different loads while learning the science behind parachute design. Lesson by Nurturing Young Mindz Foundation.
Dec 8 -nbsp;Lego Engineering ChallengeIn thisnbsp;workshop, children will be encouraged to build and solve problems. Children will learn to brainstorm and build with Lego® bricks, and then to redesign and build as they face challenges. For children ages 5 and up.

title: TeenHQ MakerSpace Studio
registrationEvidence: Pre-registration is recommended to reserve your spot.
description: Up to 5 teens at a time can use the space to utilize our 3D printers, Poster Printer, GlowForge, Sewing Serger Machines, Cricut, Button Press, and miscellaneous craft supplies.
parentSummary: Up to 5 teens at a time can use the space to utilize our 3D printers, Poster Printer, GlowForge, Sewing Serger Machines, Cricut, Button Press, and miscellaneous craft supplies.
sourceDescriptionRaw:
Middle and high schoolers: Come explore the TeenHQ MakerSpace! Up to 5 teens at a time can use the space to utilize our 3D printers, Poster Printer, GlowForge, Sewing Serger Machines, Cricut, Button Press, and miscellaneous craft supplies. Work with our teen librarian to bring your idea to life. Each machine and other materials have limitations and time requirements. Please see below for more information. Pre-registration is recommended to reserve your spot. If not all claimed registration spots have arrived by 4:30PM, they will be given to those waiting. All services are provided for free to middle and high school (6-12 grade) students. Younger people and adults are not permitted in the area unless required to assist with a disability. 
Pre-registration will start 1 week before the start of the program. Please un-register yourself if you find you're unable to attend at a later date.nbsp;Registration closes 1 hour before the start of the program. There will not be a waitlist for pre-registration. Drop-ins will be accepted if not all registration slots are filled and if not all registered individuals arrive by 4:30PM.nbsp;The area is wheelchair accessible from the Children’s Room elevator. Other accommodations can be made available with request.nbsp;ADA Accommodation RequestsPlease note that each device requires time to set up, use, and complete whatever task you're wanting to use the space for. Be sure that you have enough time in your schedule to attend the program. Not all tasks may be completed before the end of the program and you may need to return to get your completed items or pause your task and restart at another studio session. We appreciate your patience and flexibility.
3D Printing: All requested prints must take less than 4.5 hours to print. All requested prints will need to be picked up at a later date. Contact information is required for notification of pick-up. 3D print quality and time needed to complete prints is not guaranteed. Multiple objects can be printed as long as the total time does not exceed 4.5 hours. 
Poster Printing: All prints must be assembled on a 2”x3” canvas and printed as a.png. Please see the regularly scheduled poster printing event for further details. One poster per teen per day. 
GlowForge: Create a custom engraved object. Object should follow similar guidelines to the Custom Keychain Program. Complexity of request is at the discretion of the librarian. 
Sewing Serger Machines: It is recommended that you bring your own fabric and thread if fabric is special or color is a factor. There are scrap material and thread available but we cannot guarantee material quality or availability. An iron and ironing board is also available 
Cricut: Basic Cricut supplies are available, such as construction and cardstock paper. If your project is specialized, such as requiring iron-on, you’ll need to bring your own materials. It is recommended that you know the requirements for any materials you provide. 
Button Press: TeenHQ offers two sizes of button presses. We cannot offer printing. If your bring your own printout of buttons, it must be printed on standard printer paper. Paper thicker than standard printer paper cannot be used on the button presses. All measurements below are diameter length in inches. 
Small Button Press: 1.25” Large Button Press: 2.25” Picture Size: 1.156” Cut Line: 1.629” Picture Size: 2.063” Cut Line: 2.625”

sourceDescriptionRaw:
Preschool age children and their parents/caregivers are invited to the West Valley Branch Library for Reading to Children in Japanese. Every Thursday at 11:00 AM, children will enjoy early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement activities all in the Japanese language. 
This program is brought to the library by Poponta Children's Cultural Society. Established in 2008 and based in San Mateo, Poponta is comprised of a group of volunteers dedicated to serving the Japanese-speaking community. Poponta volunteers tell stories to children to open their minds to the magic of books. To learn more about Poponta, please visit:nbsp;https://ja-jp.facebook.com/popontanokai/
Free, with limited capacity. Seating is available on a first-come, first-served basis. A limited number of tickets will be distributed at the Information Desk 30 minutes prior to the start of the program. San José Public Library Early Education programs are in alignment with the City’s Education and Digital Literacy Initiative. 
 
ADA Accommodation Requests
 未就園児のお子さま、日本語に興味のあるお子さまとその保護者の皆さまは、ウェストバレーブランチ図書館日本語お話会にご参加いただけます。毎週木曜日の午前11時に、絵本の読みきかせ、手遊び歌、昔話、ペープサートなどが楽しめます。このプログラムは、ぽぽんた児童文化の会メンバーの一人と有志によって図書館で開催しています。 ぽぽんた児童文化の会は2008年に設立され、サンマテオを拠点とし、ベイエリアにお住まいの日本語を話すコミュニティに日本文化、日本語のお話を提供するボランティアグループです。パンデミック中の規則に準拠し、ストーリータイム(お話会)においてもいくつかルールが変更になりましたのでご確認ください。これは屋内プログラムになることに注意してください。全員（2歳以上）は屋内でマスク着用をお勧めします。座席は先着順でご利用いただけます。プログラム開始30分前にインフォメーションデスクにて、数量限定のチケットを配布いたします。サンノゼ公立図書館の早期教育プログラムは、市の教育およびデジタルリテラシーイニシアチブと連携しています。図書館主催のイベントでは、アメリカ障害者法に基づく介助が必要な場合、イベントの少なくとも7営業日前に408-244-4747にお電話ください。

title: Diwali Concert with Arjun Verma
description: Audiences will experience the rich heritage of North Indian classical music through traditional melodies (raagas) that capture both profound, majestic depths and exhilarating rhythms.
parentSummary: Audiences will experience the rich heritage of North Indian classical music through traditional melodies (raagas) that capture both profound, majestic depths and exhilarating rhythms.
sourceDescriptionRaw:
Celebrate the Festival of Lights with an evening of mesmerizing music featuring the acclaimed Indian-American sitarist and composer, Arjun Verma. In honor of Diwali, the Cupertino Library will host this special live performance on November 6 at 7:00 PM in Community Hall.
Hailed by the New York Times as a “fine sitarist,” Arjun Verma blends meticulous traditional training under legendary maestros like Ali Akbar Khan with a fresh, modern relevance. Audiences will experience the rich heritage of North Indian classical music through traditional melodies (raagas) that capture both profound, majestic depths and exhilarating rhythms. Whether you are a lifelong lover of classical ragas or discovering the sitar for the first time, this performance offers a beautiful, reflective space to gather and honor the spirit of Diwali through the power of sound.
This program is generously sponsored by the Cupertino Library Foundation.nbsp;
For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.

Write and Publish a Novel in a Year!
Join us for monthly writing and publishing workshops to push you through the process of crafting, finishing and publishing a novel/novella. Work independently to complete each month’s assigned word count, have one-on-one mentoring sessions, and exchange pages with your peers in a monthly critique group. Over the course of 12 months, you will create a book (minimum 17,500 words) and professionally publish it.
Completion of the novel/novella within the 12 month period is not mandatory, but If you complete your novel in the allotted timeframe, you will receive your own ISBN.
Registration required. Only 10 seats available!If you have a casual interest in writing and want to attendnbsp;certain sessions, you may join us for class without registering. However, to be eligible for an ISBN, one-on-one sessions, the critique group and to participate in the end of program Book Fair, you must register for the entire program. If you cannot make all of the sessions, but are registered and would like to remain eligible for all the perks,nbsp;you are responsible for keeping up with your monthly word commitment. You may join the program late, if there are still spaces available or someone leaves the program. sourceDescriptionRaw:
Discover how science and engineering can be used to understand and solve real environmental challenges. In this hands-on GreenRoots Collective workshop series, students will explore sustainability through interactive experiments, engineering challenges, collaborative problem-solving, and community-focused projects.
Sustainability is becoming an increasingly important part of the world students are growing up in. Understanding how the environment works, and how everyday decisions, technology, and engineering can help protect it, gives young learners the tools to think critically about real-world problems and envision better solutions for the future.
Rather than simply learning environmental concepts, students will put them into practice. Each workshop introduces a scientific idea, gives students the opportunity to investigate it through a hands-on activity, and challenges them to apply what they learn to a practical solution. Students will also contribute to community projects that connect their learning to meaningful action beyond the classroom. Through the program, participants will strengthen scientific reasoning, engineering design, creativity, teamwork, and problem-solving skills while developing a deeper understanding of sustainability and how STEM can be used to create positive change.
Series Topics:
1. Floodproof! The Science Engineering of El Niño - November 82. Cooler Cities: Engineering Solutions to Urban Heat - November 203. Clean Air Lab: The Science of Pollution Filtration - December 134. Microplastics Lab: Investigating Tiny Plastics in Our Environment - December 18

title: STEAM Sunday: Fall Sensory Bottles
description: We'll discuss density, buoyancy, mixtures, and solutions, then we'll explore what we learned as we combine ingredients for our craft.
parentSummary: We'll discuss density, buoyancy, mixtures, and solutions, then we'll explore what we learned as we combine ingredients for our craft.
sourceDescriptionRaw:
The worlds of science and art collide at STEAM Sundays.nbsp;We'll provide the supplies, you bring your curious and creative energy!
For November, we'll be celebrating the fall season as we create sensory bottles. We'll discuss density, buoyancy, mixtures, and solutions, then we'll explore what we learned as we combine ingredients for our craft. We'll also chat about seasonal changes, how they impact the world around us, and how sensory objects can help us refocus and reset. Participants will leave with their very own ready-to-use sensory bottle.
Through a brief lecture and hands-on experimenting and creating, STEAM Sundays allow participants to learn about science, technology, engineering, and math while working on an art project. After learning about a topic, the experimentation and note taking parts of the scientific process will be conducted through a craft. Everyone will go home with a finished project and better understanding of each chosen topic.
Best for youth ages 5-12.nbsp;
Supplies are limited; registration required.
STEAM Sunday:nbsp;Botellas Sensoriales de Otoño¡Los mundos de la ciencia y arte se juntan en domingos STEAM.nbsp;¡Nosotros traemos los materiales, ¡tú solo ven con muchas ganas de explorar y crear!
Este noviembre, celebraremos la temporada de otoño creando botellas sensoriales. Hablaremos sobre la densidad, la flotabilidad, las mezclas y las soluciones. Después, pondremos en práctica lo aprendido al combinar diferentes materiales para crear nuestra manualidad. También conversaremos sobre los cambios de estación, cómo afectan al mundo que nos rodea y cómo los objetos sensoriales pueden ayudarnos a recuperar la concentración y encontrar la calma.nbsp;¡Cada participante se llevará a casa su propia botella sensorial, lista para usar!A través de una breve lección, experimentos y creaciones práctica, los domingos STEAM permiten a los participantes aprender sobre ciencia, tecnología, ingeniería, y matemáticas mientras trabajan en un proyecto de arte. Después de aprender sobre cierto tema, la experimentación y el tomar apuntes de este proceso científico se llevarán a cabo por medio de una artesanía. Todos irán a casa con un proyecto terminado y con un mejor entendimiento de cada tema elegido.
Para niños y niñas de 5 a 12 años.Los materiales son limitados. Se requiere inscripción previa.

title: Giving Thanks
description: You’ll observe grassland, chaparral, and riparian habitats while discovering how local Native tribes use strategies such as cultural burning and regular pruning to nurture plants and ensure abundant food and materials for homes, baskets, and medicine.
parentSummary: You’ll observe grassland, chaparral, and riparian habitats while discovering how local Native tribes use strategies such as cultural burning and regular pruning to nurture plants and ensure abundant food and materials for homes, baskets, and medicine.
sourceDescriptionRaw: Give thanks to Native Californians by exploring how they cared for the land since time immemorial before the arrival of settler-colonialists. Join Docent Naturalists Marie Faust Evitt, Nancy Weintraub, and Megan Elmore for a moderately-paced hike along the beautiful Ipiwa, Alpine Loop, and Sunny Jim trails. You’ll observe grassland, chaparral, and riparian habitats while discovering how local Native tribes use strategies such as cultural burning and regular pruning to nurture plants and ensure abundant food and materials for homes, baskets, and medicine. Children who can comfortably hike more than four miles are welcome. Bring a snack for a break at Alpine Pond.

title: Documentaries: Holodomor Remembrance Day
description: Through compelling eyewitness accounts, the film brings into focus a pivotal and little-known period in history, the consequences of which continues to reverberate today.\nBooks on this reading listnbsp;will be on display and available.\nRegistration is not necessary, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before.
parentSummary: Through compelling eyewitness accounts, the film brings into focus a pivotal and little-known period in history, the consequences of which continues to reverberate today.\nBooks on this reading listnbsp;will be on display and available.\nRegistration is not necessary, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before.
sourceDescriptionRaw:
The Holodomor, the faminenbsp;that killed millions of Ukrainians in the 1930s, was not widely known or acknowledged until the fall of the Soviet Union in the 1990s.nbsp;Established in 1998,nbsp;Holodomor Remembrance Day is observed on the fourth Saturday of November to remember the one-quarter of Ukraine's population who died during the Holodomor.nbsp;
Join us for Palo Alto City Library's second annualnbsp;program commemorating this event and its lasting effects fornbsp;some in our community today. Three short documentaries will give us the historicalnbsp;background that reverberates innbsp;current events.nbsp;Descriptions of the documentariesnbsp;below were written by their creators.
Holodomor: How Millions of Ukrainians Died of Starvation During Stalin-Era Mass Famine (Radio Free Europe, 2019, two minutes).nbsp;Each year, on the fourth Saturday of November, Ukraine remembers the millions who died during the Holodomor, the Stalin-era famine that devastated the population in 1932-1933. Many countries consider it to have been genocide.Minnesota Memories of the Holodomornbsp;(PBS, 2025, 26 minutes).nbsp;In an extraordinary exploration of the transmission of traumatic memory within families, communities and across generations, Ukrainians in Minneapolis-St. Paul share their family stories about the Holodomor artificial famine of 1932-33 and the local community's efforts to come to terms with genocide, even as war once again threatens the existence of Ukrainians as a people. Holodomor: Voices of Survivors (2015, 30 minutes).nbsp;Twenty-five Ukrainian Canadians tell their stories of survival during the Holodomor--death inflicted by starvation--a genocide of Ukrainian people engineered by Joseph Stalin during 1932 and 1933. Through compelling eyewitness accounts, the film brings into focus a pivotal and little-known period in history, the consequences of which continues to reverberate today.
Books on this reading listnbsp;will be on display and available.
Registration is not necessary, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before.

sourceDescriptionRaw: Tidal salt marshes flood twice each day. They provide critical habitat for marine invertebrates such as oysters, mussels, and clams, shorebirds, and specialized native plants like pickleweed. Additionally, the baylands are on the Pacific Flyway, the great bird migration route between Alaska and South America. But wetlands are easy to overlook, often underappreciated, and threatened by climate change. Join Docent Naturalists Susan Bernhard, Ann Reisenauer, and Alison Hurst to explore the flora, fauna, and environmental issues of the salt marshes on this leisurely-paced, family-friendly walk along the Bay Trail.

title: Intermediate Mass Black Holes; Meteor Showers or Space Debris?
description: In this talk, we explore how changes in visible gas emission lines over nearly two decades cannbsp;reveal these hidden engines, highlighting recent Magellan Spectrograph observations of dwarf galaxy J1143 that point to an accretingnbsp;intermediate-mass black hole at its core.
parentSummary: In this talk, we explore how changes in visible gas emission lines over nearly two decades cannbsp;reveal these hidden engines, highlighting recent Magellan Spectrograph observations of dwarf galaxy J1143 that point to an accretingnbsp;intermediate-mass black hole at its core.
sourceDescriptionRaw: Lecture 1:nbsp;nbsp;Understanding how supermassive black holes grow offers key clues to how galaxies evolve, but their "missing link"—intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs)—remains elusive. Because small, blue compact dwarf galaxies cannot host supermassive monsters, theynbsp;are prime hunting grounds for IMBHs. In this talk, we explore how changes in visible gas emission lines over nearly two decades cannbsp;reveal these hidden engines, highlighting recent Magellan Spectrograph observations of dwarf galaxy J1143 that point to an accretingnbsp;intermediate-mass black hole at its core. Delivered by Kiera Aston.\nLecture 2:nbsp;nbsp;Gorgeous meteor showers streaking across the zenith, or space trash entering our atmosphere? The 21st century’s growing “spacenbsp;environment” problem is beginning to take center stage. Space debris, artificial spacecraft and objects that have ceased functioning,nbsp;are accumulating in Low Earth Orbit at an unprecedented rate. We are developing a global space debris monitoring network usingnbsp;ground-based observations. At the core of the system is a three-channel multispectral camera designed to detect the aluminumnbsp;emission line in the near-UV spectrum, providing a distinctive signature for identifying space debris as it reenters Earth’s atmosphere.nbsp;Delivered by Alice Zou.\nFor accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+days prior to the event. If you need assistance with thenbsp;form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.

title: Beyond The Spotlight: One Life. Multiple Passions. Endless Possibilities.
description: Through personal stories, practical insights, and thoughtful conversation, this event invites participants to rethink traditional career paths, make space for creativity, and redefine what success can look like.
parentSummary: Through personal stories, practical insights, and thoughtful conversation, this event invites participants to rethink traditional career paths, make space for creativity, and redefine what success can look like.
sourceDescriptionRaw: In this inspiring talk with professionals, we explore how passion for the performing arts can coexist with a primary career. Can you be a professional by day and a performer by choice? What does it look like when theater becomes more than a hobby without becoming your full-time profession? Through personal stories, practical insights, and thoughtful conversation, this event invites participants to rethink traditional career paths, make space for creativity, and redefine what success can look like. We will discuss how aspiring performers can balance education, professional goals, personal responsibilities, and their love for the stage. Join us for a thought-provoking discussion on pursuing Performing Arts and Theater as a Parallel Career Path: an exploration of passion, purpose, possibility, and the courage to embrace more than one professional identity. Carla Pantoja Carla, born and raised in the South Bay, is an actor, fight director, teaching artist, intimacy director, and mom of two. She has been a Resident Artist of San Francisco Shakespeare Festival since 2014 and recently served as Director of Vision for the 2021 Free Shakespeare in the Park production of Pericles, Prince of Tyre, directing episodes 2 and 4. In 2020, she was in the acting company at Oregon Shakespeare Festival, returning in 2022 as the festival’s first female fight director. Carla is an associate instructor for Dueling Arts International and serves on their governing body as President. She is also a proud member of Making Good Trouble, an anti-racist training cohort based in the Bay Area. Carla has directed SF Shakes Shakespeare on Tour production of Romeo and Juliet and Comedy of Errors and Assistant Directed the 2017 Free Shakespeare in the Park production of Hamlet. She played Paulina in Free Shakespeare in the Park’s The Winter’s Tale, Tybalt in Romeo and Juliet, and Kate in The Taming of the Shrew. She’s performed with Cal Shakes, Shotgun Players, Crowded Fire, Playground, Lorraine Hansberry Theatre, and the SF Mime Troupe in the Bay Area to name a few. Vinay Pande Vinay Pande is a Silicon Valley technology leader and a passionate theatre artist who brings together the worlds of innovation and performing arts. Originally from Mumbai, India, Vinay holds a degree in Instrumentation Engineering and began his career in telecommunications, where he was part of the core team that developed India’s first satellite-based mission-critical voice, data, and video network for the Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO). He later worked as a researcher at the prestigious Bell Labs and holds 15 technology patents, and co-authored technical publications and books. Today, he serves as a Principal Architect at a leading technology company in Silicon Valley. Beyond his technology career, Vinay has nurtured a deep passion for the performing arts for over a decade, actively pursuing theatre, acting, and singing across Marathi and Hindi productions. From bringing diverse characters to life on stage to engaging audiences as a Radio Jockey and event host, he thrives on the energy of live performance and the magic of storytelling. For Vinay, technology may be his profession, but the stage is where his creative spirit truly comes alive. Sowmya Renukuntla Sowmya is a Bay Area native and recent graduate from Santa Clara University, where she studied Business and worked directly with Admission Counselors for four years. Since graduating, she has been working full-time at Levi Strauss & Co. on the Corporate Insights team and is a part-time college counselor. Sponsored by the Cupertino Library Foundation. title: Festival of Lights: A Diwali Celebration
description: Noorani Dance, founded in 2016 by by international Kathak artist, Farah Yasmeen Shaikh, exemplifies Farah’s unique artistic expression and vision coupled with the classical and innovative influence and style of Farah's Guru, the late Pandit Chitresh Das.
parentSummary: Noorani Dance, founded in 2016 by by international Kathak artist, Farah Yasmeen Shaikh, exemplifies Farah’s unique artistic expression and vision coupled with the classical and innovative influence and style of Farah's Guru, the late Pandit Chitresh Das.
sourceDescriptionRaw: Join us at the Mitchell Park Community Center, as we celebrate Diwali! Enjoy fun activities for all ages including: Ongoing from 2-4 PM: Henna with teaching artist Rachel-Anne Palacios (Adobe Room; henna line closes at 3:30 PM!) Rangoli (chalk coloring craft outside in the Courtyard) Crafts (in Adobe Room) All activities available while supplies last! Performance from 2:30-3:30 PM in El Palo Alto Room by Noorani Dance. Rachel-Anne Palacios is an Afro-Chicana Oakland native, multi-cultural arts educator, and self-taught folk artist. She has been teaching art workshops and classes at Bay Area schools and libraries for over a decade and a half and her lessons and projects are inspired by indigenous cultures and traditional art from around the world. Noorani Dance, founded in 2016 by by international Kathak artist, Farah Yasmeen Shaikh, exemplifies Farah’s unique artistic expression and vision coupled with the classical and innovative influence and style of Farah's Guru, the late Pandit Chitresh Das. "Noorani" means bright or luminous, with a dual meaning of enlightenment. With Kathak dance as their medium, Noorani Dance is committed to enlightening minds and hearts through the arts.

sourceDescriptionRaw: | Performances: December 2-3, 2026 | A holiday mash-up for the whole family, The Hip Hop Nutcracker returns for another spectacular tour. Directed and choreographed by Tony and Olivier Award-nominated Jennifer Weber, this contemporary dance spectacle is a re-mixed and re-imagined version of the classic, smashing hip hop dance and Tchaikovsky’s timeless music together into a heart-stirring and inspirational holiday event. The Hip Hop Nutcracker is brought to life by a powerhouse cast of a dozen all-star dancers, a DJ, a violinist, and MC Kurtis Blow, one of hip hop’s founding fathers, who opens the show with a short set. Just like the original, in The Hip Hop Nutcracker, Maria-Clara and the Nutcracker Prince go on a dream adventure battling a gang of mice, visiting the land of sweets and learning the lessons of the holiday season. Innovative digital graffiti and visuals transform the landscape of E.T.A. Hoffmann’s beloved story from traditional 19th Century Germany to the vibrant, diverse sights and sounds of contemporary New York City. Grab your family and friends and let the dynamic performers of The Hip Hop Nutcracker take you on a journey that celebrates love, community and the magic of the holiday season. Performances: ● Wed., December 2, 2026 @ 7:00pm ● Thur., December 3, 2026 @ 7:00pm > CPA Events Calendar > Visitor FAQs

sourceDescriptionRaw: Sunday, March 7, 2027 at 11 a.m. California Theatre, San Jose, CA Concert Length Approx. 55 minutes No intermission $25 - Child $40 - Adult Monique Hafen Adams, narrator Symphony San Jose The Young Person’s Guide to the Orchestra My Very First Symphony is a special one-hour concert presented by Symphony San Jose featuring Britten’s The Young Person’s Guide to the Orchestra, ideal for families with toddlers, preschoolers, and young children. Brilliantly inventive and endlessly engaging, Britten’s The Young Person’s Guide to the Orchestra takes listeners on a tour of the ensemble, revealing how the personality of each instrument and their respective families contribute to the symphonic sound. Introducing children to classical music opens a world of imagination, emotion, and discovery. Live orchestral performances captivate young minds with vibrant sounds, dynamic storytelling, and the magic of musicians creating music together in real time. These early experiences spark curiosity, build listening skills, and create lasting memories that can inspire a lifelong love of music and the arts. Children aged one year and older require a ticket for entry. No furry friends here—just something even better! Our instrument petting zoo lets little hands explore real orchestral instruments up close. Kids can touch a violin, tap on percussion, and discover the sounds that bring music to life. It’s a fun, interactive way to turn curious toddlers into engaged listeners before the concert even starts. Join us one hour prior to the concert and let the musical adventure begin! title: Disney's Dare to Dream Jr.
description: As the trainees work together to discover their own dreams, they uncover the power that imagination and teamwork have to make anything possible.
parentSummary: As the trainees work together to discover their own dreams, they uncover the power that imagination and teamwork have to make anything possible.
sourceDescriptionRaw: | Performances: June 23-27 | Children's Musical Theater San Jose (CMT San Jose) presents Disney's Dare to Dream JR., a musical revue that follows an eager group of trainees on their first day at a fictional Walt Disney Imagineering Studio. As the trainees work together to discover their own dreams, they uncover the power that imagination and teamwork have to make anything possible. Celebrating 100 years of Disney music, the production features 20 songs spanning a century of beloved films, including selections making their stage debut alongside favorites from The Princess and the Frog, Coco, Encanto, and Frozen II. Now in its 59th season, CMT San Jose is one of the region's premier youth performing arts organizations, offering training and performance opportunities to thousands of young artists each year. CMT San Jose trains and educates today's youth through musical theater to set and achieve high artistic and personal goals, and to inspire them to become exemplary artists, patrons and citizens of tomorrow. The organization is dedicated to fostering creativity and a lifelong love of the performing arts in a supportive and inclusive environment.
